utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry. It's just coming up now. Just bear with us for a second. It will be with you in just one moment, Professor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Page 38 -- oh, in the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Let me read the sentence to you. It says: "About ten metres further downstream from R-24, a pair of trousers with leg bones inside the pant legs and a black jacket were found and were marked with R-26." So it would appear from your statement - correct me if I'm wrong - that both R-26 and R-27 have been described by you in the 92 ter statement as "a pair of trousers with leg bones inside the pant legs and a black jacket." Is that the position? Is that what they both were? Can you help us at all?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were two completely different numbers -- or rather, two different locations. On one location, mortal remains labeled with number 26 were found; and another location, where mortal remains labeled with number 27 were found.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. And in your statement you say both of those sets of mortal remains consisted of a pair of trousers with leg bones inside the pant legs and a black jacket. That's correct, is it?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Look, I don't exclude the possibility that speaking as a witness from my memory I made an error in my statement. What I wrote in my daily report is correct. That's the most reliable record. With number 26, trousers were found; in one trouser leg, bone fragments were found and a black jacket. And next to number 27, pieces of clothing were found, two human ankles, a shoulder blade.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: And the witness said something that the interpreter didn't catch.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's true. And that's the only accurate record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Could you repeat what was found in R-27. It was not translated completely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you -- you said two human ankles, a shoulder blade, and then we missed what you then said.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. Is the question directed at me? I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We did not fully -- or the interpreters didn't fully --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Under number 27, the pieces of clothing were found, two human shin bones, left shoulder blade, and a part of the spinal column. As far as I recall, this is clearly visible in the photographic documentation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it is. It even appears that some ribs are there as well, if I interpret the picture well. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Those are my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Emmerson. Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Part of the ribs that run along the spinal column. That's probably what it relates to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'd like to understand something, if I could. You just said with regard to the questioning of Mr. Emmerson: "That's true. And that's the only accurate record," referring, I take it, to your daily report. My question -- my question to you is: Did you read your 92 ter statement before you signed it, sir?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In principle I leafed through it. However, as you can see, I signed the corrigendum a few days ago pertaining to some typos; therefore, one cannot be certain that a typo or two slipped by.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, I think that we've been discussing something a bit more than typos. And you've now said that in -- in principle you leafed through it. I'll ask you the question again: Did you read your 92 ter statement before you signed it, sir?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did, as far as I recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. Before you went to the area where you conducted your investigation, you received information that the police had been there for at least a couple of days before you arrived; correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And you had an opportunity to speak, I believe, with Judge Gojkovic, who was the investigating judge in charge of the area. True?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And correct me if I'm wrong, sir, the manner in which the process for the investigation of the area was divided was that the police and the investigating judge were responsible for mapping and diagramming the area, photographing the area, and otherwise memorialising the general site. Correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was the modus operandi in principle. That is how it should be done.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And you were specifically involved in reviewing remains in their various stages throughout the area; correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, when you arrived in the area, was the entire area cordoned off?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can tell you that I did see some tapes; although, I don't remember exactly where. I remember seeing them as we were arriving from a car or a jeep. There were those police yellow/red tapes around.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Were you given when you arrived in the area a diagram of what the police had observed before you came to the area some days after they first arrived?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. As soon as we arrived, we were taken there by the police. We saw a group of corpses next to the canal immediately, and we saw an overturned vehicle, a passenger car together with the corpse number 18 that burnt down.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Sir, my question was: Were you provided a diagram? And you've answered the question. Before you went to the area, were you --

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can briefly tell you no. After being at the canal, we went to the farm, where we saw --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Let me -- let me stop you there. Mr. Guy-Smith had asked you a question whether you were provided with something. Your answer is "no." He was not seeking at this moment in full detail what you then did. If he's interested, he'll certainly ask you. Mr. Guy-Smith, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you were tasked or sent to engage in this investigation, were you aware of a document entitled "The United Nations Manual on the Effective Prevention and Investigation of Extra-Legal, Arbitrary and Summary Executions," which was passed by the United Nations in 1991, also known as the Minnesota Protocol?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I am not.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, if that's the case, then there are a series of questions that I won't ask you about that document, which sets the minimum standards for various forms of investigations.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You were asked some questions by Mr. Emmerson with regard to recovery of lead from the wall. I want to ask you a question as to whether or not you directed recovery of any material whatsoever from the wall or any concrete fragments for purposes of examination.

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I'm a medical doctor, and I only directed the recovery of bodies and anything that had to do with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did you direct for the recovery of any soil samples whatsoever for purposes of examination and investigation? I assume your answer will be the same, which is that you're a medical -- a medical doctor.

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not direct anything. I did not see any inconsistencies or differences that I deemed important. Otherwise, had I been able to see that there was something consistent about the soil, I would have directed such an inquiry.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, just for purposes of clarification, have you taken courses with regard to different soils and the composition of soil? And by that I'm referring specifically with regard to the soil that could be found at the top of a canyon, as opposed to the soil material that would be found at the bottom of a canyon. And my -- my question is: Have you received any training in that area? Taken any courses in that area?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, as a medical doctor my work had to do with the corpses and things immediately connected to that. When I mentioned the soil, I meant only the soil that was immediately next to the corpses. We have to secure biological traces and other traces for any further potential analysis. In terms of specific courses, no, I have no training in that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That last line is an answer to the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And with regard to the -- with regard to the specific issue of vegetation, I take it that your answer would be the same in terms of an expertise of the type of flora that grows at various positions in a canal area; right?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: My question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Neither do I, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, if nobody understands the question, I better ask it again quickly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please reformulate.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to the issue of -- of flora, plants, I take it you have no expertise with regard to the type of plants that would grow at any particular point in the canyon that you were examining. And by that I mean plants that are closer to the water, plants that are higher up on the wall, as opposed to plants that are closer to the flat area where the land may be drier.

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not an expert in plants, be it the plants growing there or here in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Very well. With regard to the issue of vegetation, do you have any expertise with regard to vegetation growing in a body? And by that I mean the vegetation entangled and intertwined with a dead body.

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I don't understand the question. However, I can tell you this: We saw no vegetation that would go through the corpses. Maybe there were some plants that would grow between the arm and the main part of the body, which reminds me of the photograph concerning the body number 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I have no questions about body number 5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I do have a question with regard to issues concerning hydrology.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And this is something I raised before in my question. My question here is:

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You've mentioned -- you mentioned that at least with regard to a body being desiccated, it is -- it is lighter, so it could move with greater ease. Could you tell us whether or not you have conducted any experiments or have any expertise in the amount of hydrological force is required to move a body down a slope?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for any loss of weight, I did study that from our professional sources. As for the other part of the question, I'm not an expert in that. However, I saw what the torrent looked like on the 13th and I saw it wash away everything in its path, including the rocks outside the canal, on -- in the places where on the previous day we had moved some bodies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, I'm looking at the clock. Would you have any further questions or -- because you're on a rather theoretical level on what the witness has not studied.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, to the extent that the witness has -- has drawn opinions or conclusions involving these matters, to the extent that the witness has not studied these matters, it may be -- it may be germane to the Chamber. And I think I've covered flora; I've covered soil; I've covered hydrology. And we understand that no further materials of, let's say, a harder substance - by that I mean concrete, rock, or any form of metal material - were recovered with regard to this investigation. And I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey, you had one question, you told us.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Sorry to disappoint. I have -- I have to decided not to ask it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Harvey. Mr. Dutertre, I'm looking at the clock. I'm also looking at the booth. I want to give you an opportunity to put one or two questions. We are entering into a lot of detail which might not be -- or which shed some slight on precision, which sheds some light on limits of expertise, which sheds some light on probabilities to be distinguished from certainties, errors, et cetera. I think that we could go on with that for -- for a couple of hours - "a couple of hours" being two hours, I now understand - but if there's anything really bothering you, please take the opportunity, with the indulgence of interpreters and technicians, for just a couple of minutes, not more. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I shall try to be brief and I would like the witness to answer briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Professor, you re-read your 92 ter interview in your own language, in Serbian, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: You were at the scene to recover the bodies every day. Mr. Dunjic was for the main part at Hotel Pastrik conducting the post-mortem examination.

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: You mentioned the very strong current on the 12th, 13th -- 13th, 14th, and 15th. Given that the current was so strong, could some of the bodies have been carried into the lake?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where from? Theoretically it is possible, but on the 11th and the 12th we cleared the plateau. The torrent was not on the 13th, 14th, and the 15th, but the strongest one was on the 13th, somewhat less on the 14th, and on the 15th we were already working inside the canal.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: So I'm referring to the 13th.

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the body was in a different place. But the part that we had cleared was clear of any bodies. We didn't go back to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: I'm talking about the bodies that were found in the canyon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Simply this. I'm not sure that Mr. Dutertre has called it to mind, but the document that the witness was shown earlier on the divers' report --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- which he said he accepted, catered for the possibility of the heaviest possible torrent and was completed afterwards --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You can ask yourself what the level of the expertise of the divers is or the level of experience. That is all rather vague, both, everything. I mean, if someone would have to -- to forecast what happened during the tsunami, then everyone would have said that certain things would have been totally impossible, which turned out not to be impossible. We do not know a lot of the exact circumstances. So therefore we are doing it with this for the time being.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. And I'd simply put it in those -- in those circumstances.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'd put it as an objection to the eliciting of an opinion outside the witness's expertise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Dutertre, while the witness has answer the question already, which leaves the issue of his expertise, and the Chamber, of course, will have to deal with that. Mr. Dutertre, next question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, as far as the 15th is concerned, Mr. Emmerson put to you questions about a body 700 metres away, as opposed to the entrance to the canal, and you said that that was body R-20. I don't have the transcript before me. Wouldn't it be body R-28? Are you quite sure that this was body R-20?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If in the police report there is a description of the body being stuck underneath a rock, in my report the body that was stuck underneath a rock was the body number 20. I have to refer to the documents then.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: I'll put the question differently to go faster. Was body R-20 recovered on the 15th of September or before that date?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before that. It was recovered on the 12th.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you. Apart from body R-1, you thought that body R-1 came from elsewhere. Did you notice anything, anything which would make you believe that these bodies R-2 from R-17 came from elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I described such indications, the most important being the way the soil was mixed with the bodies. As I like to say, the bodies were merged or -- or joined with the soil. Having in mind all that and having in mind that I wasn't there alone and that it wasn't only my impression, the conclusion is such. I don't want to talk about the impressions of certain people who were not professionals in our field, such as the divers, but I'm talking about my colleague Mr. Jecmenica. The most important thing was the impression that was there and that can be also seen on the footage.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: If I've understood you correctly, you are saying - I would just like to clarify this - you said according to you the bodies had been there for a number of weeks. I understand that you couldn't tell us exactly for how many weeks, two, four, five, or six. You can't tell us, can you?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Very well. And this is my last question. I would like to bring up document P749, page 3 on the screen. These are post-mortem examination photographs relating to body R-27. Perhaps you could enlarge this, please. Professor Aleksandric, can you confirm that this is a black jacket which you see on the screen?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. In my daily report, I described it as parts of clothing, because of the mud I wasn't able to establish what piece of clothing exactly it is. Only once it was washed and dried at the Pastrik Hotel did we realise which particular item it was, and then it was marked with the same number.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Dutertre. May I take it that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that the Defence has no need to put further questions triggered by the re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Since the Chamber also has no questions to you, Professor Aleksandric - please be careful - since we have no further questions to you either, I'd like to thank you very much for coming not only once but coming twice to The Hague and answer all questions put to you by the parties and by the Bench. We're happy that we could conclude today and I wish you a safe trip home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Madam Usher, would you escort the witness out of the courtroom. Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I know it's late in the evening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I received -- I received a message. I wanted to indicate to the Chamber that the matter of perfection of the record has been dealt with by us filing a document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: It should take care of all those things. And that's what I meant by that and I just wanted to ensure the Chamber that there were no difficulties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It was not entirely clear to me from your request whether we would have to do something or whether the mere fact that your request was filed finally --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- met your concerns.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No. I just wanted to take that -- I wanted to take that off the long, long list that I know each one of us has.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then when I earlier gave you until Friday -- I said "preferably not 10.00 at night"- to respond to -- to the request for protective measures for the witness to appear next -- next week Monday, I had overlooked a specific request of one of my colleagues, who said since it might be a more-than-usual difficult issue here, that if you would by filing a bit early would give us some additional time to consider the matter and not rush into the Monday morning, then that would be highly appreciated. I gave you until Friday evening. But if you could do it any quicker, it would really be appreciated.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Most definitely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then -- oh, no, I've -- we adjourn until Monday, quarter past 2.00. And Mr. Registrar gave me the -- all the information, but I spoiled it. I think it's quarter past 2.00 in this same courtroom, Mr. Registrar? Yes, until Monday, quarter past 2.00, same courtroom.
